prize_parts.citation: For the discovery that liquid-liquid phase separation, driven by multivalent molecular interactions, organizes the interior of living cells into biomolecular condensates.

statement.case_for: Biomolecular condensates replaced the picture of the cell interior as a bag of membrane-bound compartments with a physical-chemical principle: demixing, multivalency and phase boundaries produce membraneless organization. Hyman and Brangwynne showed P granules and nucleoli behave as liquids; Rosen supplied the quantitative multivalent-domain framework. The concept is general, originated in chemistry-adjacent physics, has been reproduced by many independent groups, and connects directly to aggregation and amyloid-like transitions. It is a new concept of molecular organization, which I value more than a new tool.
statement.case_against: The in vivo picture is still contested: which condensates are genuinely liquid, which are gels or aggregates, and which are functionally relevant. Critics argue that some of the cellular evidence rests on overexpression, and 'phase separation' is sometimes used loosely. The boundary of credit is also unsettled, because Pappu and Mittag on sequence grammar are left out of a three-person cut. A reasonable colleague could call the field more cell biology than chemistry and the verdict premature.

responses.point: Targeted protein degradation (B045) turned the ubiquitin-proteasome system into a designable chemical modality, with Crews, Deshaies and Handa as the core and clinical-stage degraders already in progress.
responses.response: I ranked B045 fourth in my opening and still rate it as a real new concept. I disagree that it is the strongest case now. No PROTAC drug is approved, and the Crews, Deshaies, Handa trio leaves out Ciulli, Sakamoto and Gray, so both timing and attribution are weaker than you suggest. I would also separate the glue branch, which is mature, from the PROTAC branch, which is not. Phase separation is at least as widely replicated, and its physical-chemical grounding is firmer.

responses.point: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B009) are the game-changing chemistry behind siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines, and Cullis is the most defensible core of any configuration.
responses.response: This is the strongest challenge to my first choice, and as a lipid self-assembly person I take it seriously. The impact is demonstrated at planetary scale and the maturity is higher than condensates. I agree Cullis is the defensible core. My hesitation is that the credit among Vancouver formulation work, Anderson and Langer's lipidoid libraries, and MacLachlan's lipid design is hard to cut cleanly into three names, and the delivery story sits close to the 2023 mRNA prize. I keep it as my first alternative, and I could move to it if the committee judges concept less decisive than consequence.

responses.point: Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling (B069) is a mature, overdue, molecule-making achievement with a clean Buchwald and Hartwig pair, and chemistry should reward demonstrated breadth of use.
responses.response: I accept the maturity and the clean attribution, and I would not call it undeserving. My qualification is about balance. Synthetic methodology has a deep bench of strong candidates, while a physical-chemical concept that changed how a whole field thinks has fewer routes to recognition. Given the 2010 cross-coupling prize and the 2021 organocatalysis prize, a second Pd coupling award is also more incremental conceptually than condensates. I would rank B069 well but not first.

responses.point: Long-range electron transfer through proteins (B006) is a foundational physical-chemical result with a clean two-person attribution to Gray and Winkler, and recognition is not premature.
responses.response: I share your preference for quantitative physical-chemical mechanism, and B006 has cleaner credit and a longer track record than condensates. I did not rank it in my opening, which I now think undervalued it. The reason I still put condensates ahead is breadth of reorganization of a field, since electron-transfer tunneling builds on Marcus theory recognized in 1992 and is felt mainly within bioinorganic and bioenergetic chemistry. I would support B006 in a two-part configuration if the committee wants an older physical-chemistry achievement.

uncertainties: How much of the in vivo condensate evidence the committee regards as settled versus still maturing
Whether Pappu and Mittag should displace Rosen or Brangwynne given the three-person limit
Whether the committee sees B008 as chemistry rather than cell biology
Whether a lipid-nanoparticle part (Cullis) could be paired with condensates without an arbitrary split of credit
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for the shortlisted candidates. I work on lipid self-assembly and amyloid, which overlaps scientifically with B008 and B009, but I have no stated personal or institutional tie to any credited person. Lund colleagues Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai are on the committee, but none of their stated interests relate to my top candidates.
